name: vehicle–track coupled dynamics
definition_zh: 研究车辆与轨道相互作用及振动的动力学理论与分析框架。
usage_note: 所引文献使用 coupled dynamics，也有 coupling dynamics 的写法；引用时应保留原文表达。
usage_overview: 通过轮轨相互作用联立车辆与轨道的运动方程，计算双方振动及相互影响，为轨道隔振性能、参数匹配等分析提供基础，也可扩展至包含隧道或其他下部结构的系统动力分析。

complete_examples.text: Keywords Floating slab track, vibration isolation performance, fractional derivative, stochastic analysis, vehicle–track coupled dynamics, number theoretical method, probability density evolution method Date received: 13 October 2018; accepted: 15 September 2019 Introduction Due to the advantages of large capacity, speed and punctuality, and the ability to significantly alleviate traffic congestion as well as pollution in urban areas,1 the metro system has been one of the most popular solutions for large cities in order to deal with urban transportation problems.

Based on the vehicle–track coupled dynamics theory [18, 19], the wheel–rail lateral coupling matrices have been derived by energy variation principle in [25], which can be introduced to this model accordingly.

As a supplement to the vehicle–track coupled dynamics method in [18] and following the convenience of modelling of finite element system, the wheel–rail interaction is characterized by matrix coupling formulations in energy principle instead of deriving wheel–rail forces explicitly.
The vehicle–track coupled system is established in light of vehicle–track coupled dynamics theory.
In this work, matrix formulations for revealing vehicle– track–tunnel dynamic interaction mechanisms are presented in light of the methodology of vehicle–track coupled dynamics [20].
Based on the theory of vehicle–track coupled dynamics [34–36], the vehicle and the track can be treated as an integrated system through wheel–rail dynamic interactions.

In the past three decades, vehicle–track coupled dynamics has gradually matured, and more researchers have expanded the application range of this theory from the perspective of system dynamics (Chen, 2021; Di et al., 2018).

The vehicle–track system can be divided into vehicle system, track structure, and wheel–rail interaction system, which are described by multi-body dynamics, finite element method, and vehicle–track coupled dynamics, respectively.
